title: What is known about 1RB0RD_1RC1RB_1LD0LA_1LE0RA_0LF---_0LA0LC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RD_1RC1RB_1LD0LA_1LE0RA_0LF---_0LA0LC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. A region at the fixed end is ticked once per sweep of a growing wall of 8-cell words (the wall crossings are proved in Lean); the tick rule has not been extracted yet.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 31,812 cells have been visited and 16,003 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Shift rules of the sweep
claims.text: For every n and any tape around: the head crosses the wall of words 00101011 and its rewritten forms, rewriting every word the same way.

claims.title: A counter ticked by the sweeps
claims.text: Read off the simulation: apart from the growing wall, only a region at the right end changes, and only rarely, like the digits of a counter.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It depends on the tick rule of the right region, not yet extracted.

claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LD_0RC---_0RD0RF_1LE0LA_1LF1LE_1RA0RD up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0RE_1RC0LE_0RD---_0RE0RA_1LF0LB_1LA1LF up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. A wall of 8-cell words grows at the left end of the tape. On every sweep the head zigzags across it, rewriting each word on the way. At the right end, a short region of altered words changes now and then, like a counter that the sweeps are ticking.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 31,812 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The head's zigzag across the wall, proved in Lean.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.486). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 31,812 cells (20,259 left of the start, 109 right), with a density of 1s of 0.503.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A wall and a counter
html: Three million steps in, the tape is a wall of words 00101011 followed by a mixed region. Going right, the head zigzags across each word in 36 steps and turns it into 10001111. The wall keeps growing at its left end. Those crossings are proved in Lean.
Only the region at the right end changes from one sweep to the next, and only rarely. The open question is the rule by which it is ticked.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0LD_0RC---_0RD0RF_1LE0LA_1LF1LE_1RA0RD: rename A→D, B→E, C→F, D→A, E→B, F→C and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state D, in a mirror
  • 1RB0RE_1RC0LE_0RD---_0RE0RA_1LF0LB_1LA1LF: rename A→E, B→F, C→A, D→B, E→C, F→D and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state C, in a mirror

summary: A wall of 8-cell words grows at the left end and the head crosses it every sweep, rewriting each word (the crossings are proved in Lean); a region of mixed words at the right end changes rarely, like a counter. The tick rule has not been extracted.
